output: html_document

# Purpose

No new INLA severity model is fitted here.

The revised framework retains the completed continuous transmission and severity quantities and
adds the product-specific Step 11 metrics required for the two-product communication layer:

1. `T_i`: recent transmission intensity, defined as mean posterior IRR in 2024-2025.
2. `V_i`: age-weighted severity vulnerability, defined as the municipality age-composition-weighted national age-specific observed CFR.
3. `B_i`: all-age combined transmission-severity burden score, defined as `T_i` multiplied by the population-weighted severity burden.
4. `Metric_A`: deployable 18-59 burden score, `T_i * sum_{a=18-59}(P_ia * CFR_a)`.
5. `Metric_B`: older-adult 60+ burden score, `T_i * sum_{a>=60}(P_ia * CFR_a)`.

All burden scores are relative prioritization scores because `T_i` is a posterior relative incidence
measure rather than a calibrated absolute incidence prediction. They must not be interpreted as
predicted numbers of deaths.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
source("00_setup.R")

results_dir <- RESULTS_DIR
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# 1. Load completed inputs

This step uses the already-completed population panels and INLA posterior rates. It does not refit the spatiotemporal model.

```{r load-inputs}
if (!exists("pop_panel_total")) {
  if (!file.exists(result_path("pop_panel_total.rds"))) stop("pop_panel_total.rds not found.")
  pop_panel_total <- readRDS(result_path("pop_panel_total.rds"))
}

if (!exists("pop_panel_age")) {
  if (!file.exists(result_path("pop_panel_age.rds"))) stop("pop_panel_age.rds not found.")
  pop_panel_age <- readRDS(result_path("pop_panel_age.rds"))
}

st_rate_path <- file.path(results_dir, "st_rate_chik_region_2016_2025.rds")

if (!exists("st_rate_chik_region")) {
  if (!file.exists(st_rate_path)) {
    stop("st_rate_chik_region_2016_2025.rds not found in RESULTS_DIR: ", RESULTS_DIR)
  }
  st_rate_chik_region <- readRDS(st_rate_path)
}

if (!exists("Chik_total")) {
  stop("Chik_total is not in memory. Run the revised 01_data_import_cleaning.Rmd first.")
}

if (!exists("decode_age_years")) {
  decode_age_years <- function(NU_IDADE_N) {
    unit_code <- floor(NU_IDADE_N / 1000)
    value <- NU_IDADE_N %% 1000
    dplyr::case_when(
      unit_code == 1 ~ value / (24 * 365),
      unit_code == 2 ~ value / 365,
      unit_code == 3 ~ value / 12,
      unit_code == 4 ~ value,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  }
}

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(st_rate_chik_region$code_muni) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(pop_panel_total$code_muni) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(pop_panel_age$code_muni) == 5570L
)

cat("INLA rate rows:", nrow(st_rate_chik_region), "\n")
cat("INLA municipalities:", n_distinct(st_rate_chik_region$code_muni), "\n")
cat("Population municipalities:", n_distinct(pop_panel_age$code_muni), "\n")
```

# 2. National age-specific observed CFR, 2016-2025

The main severity weights use the full study period. Six age bands are used so that the strong increase in observed fatality with older age is not collapsed into a single 65+ category.

```{r cfr-weights}
chik_severity <- Chik_total %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)),
    age_years = decode_age_years(NU_IDADE_N),
    age_band = case_when(
      !is.na(age_years) & age_years < 18 ~ "0-17",
      age_years >= 18 & age_years < 40 ~ "18-39",
      age_years >= 40 & age_years < 60 ~ "40-59",
      age_years >= 60 & age_years < 70 ~ "60-69",
      age_years >= 70 & age_years < 80 ~ "70-79",
      age_years >= 80 ~ "80+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    death = as.integer(as.character(EVOLUCAO) == "2")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    year %in% 2016:2025,
    CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
    !is.na(age_band)
  )

cfr_weights <- chik_severity %>%
  group_by(age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = n(),
    deaths = sum(death, na.rm = TRUE),
    CFR = deaths / cases,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    age_band = factor(
      age_band,
      levels = c("0-17", "18-39", "40-59", "60-69", "70-79", "80+")
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(age_band)

print(cfr_weights)
```

# 3. Recent transmission intensity, 2024-2025

`T_i` is the municipality mean of the monthly posterior IRR during 2024-2025, matching the recent targeting window used by the priority framework.

```{r transmission-2024-2025}
transmission_source_2425 <- st_rate_chik_region %>%
  mutate(ym_date = as.Date(ym_date)) %>%
  filter(lubridate::year(ym_date) %in% c(2024, 2025))

transmission_check <- transmission_source_2425 %>%
  count(code_muni, name = "n_months")

stopifnot(
  nrow(transmission_check) == 5570L,
  all(transmission_check$n_months == 24L)
)

transmission_2425 <- transmission_source_2425 %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    T_irr = mean(IRR),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(transmission_2425) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(transmission_2425$code_muni) == 5570L,
  !anyDuplicated(transmission_2425$code_muni),
  all(is.finite(transmission_2425$T_irr))
)

summary(transmission_2425$T_irr)
```

# 4. Municipality age composition, 2024-2025

Population is averaged across 2024 and 2025 within each age band before calculating the municipality age composition.

```{r population-age-2024-2025}
pop_age_2425 <- pop_panel_age %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2024, 2025)) %>%
  mutate(
    age_band = case_when(
      age < 18 ~ "0-17",
      age >= 18 & age < 40 ~ "18-39",
      age >= 40 & age < 60 ~ "40-59",
      age >= 60 & age < 70 ~ "60-69",
      age >= 70 & age < 80 ~ "70-79",
      age >= 80 ~ "80+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year, age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pop = mean(pop),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

coverage_check <- pop_age_2425 %>%
  count(code_muni, name = "n_age_bands")

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(pop_age_2425$code_muni) == 5570L,
  all(coverage_check$n_age_bands == 6L)
)
```

# 5. Severity vulnerability and population-weighted severity burden

For municipality `i` and age group `a`,

`w_ia = P_ia / P_i`

and the age-weighted severity vulnerability score is

`V_i = sum_a(w_ia * CFR_a)`.

The population-weighted severity burden component is

`S_i = sum_a(P_ia * CFR_a)`.

`V_i` removes municipality population size from the severity axis. `S_i` intentionally retains population size and is used only in the combined burden score.

```{r severity-metrics}
severity_muni <- pop_age_2425 %>%
  left_join(
    cfr_weights %>% select(age_band, CFR),
    by = "age_band"
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  mutate(
    total_pop = sum(mean_pop),
    w_age = mean_pop / total_pop
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop = first(total_pop),
    V_risk = sum(w_age * CFR),
    V_burden = sum(mean_pop * CFR),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(severity_muni) == 5570L,
  sum(is.na(severity_muni$V_risk)) == 0L,
  sum(is.na(severity_muni$V_burden)) == 0L
)

cat("Spearman V_burden vs population:",
    cor(severity_muni$V_burden, severity_muni$total_pop,
        method = "spearman"), "\n")
cat("Spearman V_risk vs population:",
    cor(severity_muni$V_risk, severity_muni$total_pop,
        method = "spearman"), "\n")

summary(severity_muni$V_risk)
summary(severity_muni$V_burden)
```

# 6. Combined transmission-severity burden score

The combined score is

`B_i = T_i * S_i`.

Because `T_i` is a relative posterior IRR rather than an absolute predicted incidence, `B_i` is an uncalibrated prioritization score and must not be interpreted as a predicted number of deaths.

```{r combined-score}
priority_metric_2425 <- transmission_2425 %>%
  left_join(severity_muni, by = "code_muni") %>%
  mutate(
    combined_burden = T_irr * V_burden,
    code_state = substr(code_muni, 1, 2)
  ) %>%
  left_join(state_region_lookup, by = "code_state")

stopifnot(
  nrow(priority_metric_2425) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(priority_metric_2425$code_muni) == 5570L,
  !anyDuplicated(priority_metric_2425$code_muni),
  all(is.finite(priority_metric_2425$T_irr)),
  all(is.finite(priority_metric_2425$V_risk)),
  all(is.finite(priority_metric_2425$V_burden)),
  all(is.finite(priority_metric_2425$combined_burden)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    priority_metric_2425$combined_burden,
    priority_metric_2425$T_irr * priority_metric_2425$V_burden
  ))
)

summary(priority_metric_2425$combined_burden)
```


# 6A. Product-specific expected-burden metrics

Ana's Step 11 distinguishes the population currently eligible for the licensed product
(ages 18-59) from adults aged 60 years and older, who are excluded from that product but
are the target population for the second-product policy scenario.

For each municipality, the age-specific population-weighted severity components are

`S_Ai = sum_{a in 18-59}(P_ia * CFR_a)`

and

`S_Bi = sum_{a >= 60}(P_ia * CFR_a)`.

The two continuous prioritization scores are

`Metric_Ai = T_i * S_Ai`

and

`Metric_Bi = T_i * S_Bi`.

These are relative expected-burden scores, not calibrated expected death counts.

```{r product-specific-metrics}
product_burden_components <- pop_age_2425 %>%
  left_join(
    cfr_weights %>%
      select(
        age_band,
        CFR
      ),
    by = "age_band"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    product_group = case_when(
      age_band %in%
        c("18-39", "40-59") ~
        "A_18_59",
      age_band %in%
        c("60-69", "70-79", "80+") ~
        "B_60plus",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    weighted_severity =
      mean_pop * CFR
  ) %>%
  filter(
    product_group %in%
      c("A_18_59", "B_60plus")
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    code_muni,
    product_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    severity_burden_component =
      sum(
        weighted_severity,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    product_population =
      sum(
        mean_pop,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = product_group,
    values_from = c(
      severity_burden_component,
      product_population
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    S_A_18_59 =
      severity_burden_component_A_18_59,
    S_B_60plus =
      severity_burden_component_B_60plus,
    pop_A_18_59 =
      product_population_A_18_59,
    pop_B_60plus =
      product_population_B_60plus
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(product_burden_components) == 5570L,
  all(
    is.finite(
      product_burden_components$
        S_A_18_59
    )
  ),
  all(
    is.finite(
      product_burden_components$
        S_B_60plus
    )
  ),
  all(
    product_burden_components$
      S_A_18_59 >= 0
  ),
  all(
    product_burden_components$
      S_B_60plus >= 0
  )
)

priority_metric_2425 <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  left_join(
    product_burden_components,
    by = "code_muni"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Metric_A =
      T_irr * S_A_18_59,
    Metric_B =
      T_irr * S_B_60plus
  )

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(priority_metric_2425$Metric_A),
  !anyNA(priority_metric_2425$Metric_B),
  all(
    is.finite(
      priority_metric_2425$Metric_A
    )
  ),
  all(
    is.finite(
      priority_metric_2425$Metric_B
    )
  )
)

cat(
  "Spearman Metric A vs transmission-only:",
  cor(
    priority_metric_2425$Metric_A,
    priority_metric_2425$T_irr,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Spearman Metric B vs transmission-only:",
  cor(
    priority_metric_2425$Metric_B,
    priority_metric_2425$T_irr,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Spearman Metric A vs Metric B:",
  cor(
    priority_metric_2425$Metric_A,
    priority_metric_2425$Metric_B,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

# 6B. Continuous-ranking concordance and difference

Raw Metric A and Metric B values are not directly comparable because their age windows and
severity scales differ. For the map of disagreement, compare percentile ranks rather than raw
scores.

```{r product-rank-concordance}
priority_metric_2425 <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  mutate(
    rank_A =
      rank(
        -Metric_A,
        ties.method = "average"
      ),
    rank_B =
      rank(
        -Metric_B,
        ties.method = "average"
      ),
    pct_A =
      1 -
      (
        rank_A - 1
      ) /
      (
        n() - 1
      ),
    pct_B =
      1 -
      (
        rank_B - 1
      ) /
      (
        n() - 1
      ),
    rank_percentile_difference =
      pct_A - pct_B
  )

rank_concordance_two_product <-
  tibble::tibble(
    comparison = c(
      "Metric A vs Metric B",
      "Metric A vs transmission-only",
      "Metric B vs transmission-only"
    ),
    spearman_rho = c(
      cor(
        priority_metric_2425$Metric_A,
        priority_metric_2425$Metric_B,
        method = "spearman"
      ),
      cor(
        priority_metric_2425$Metric_A,
        priority_metric_2425$T_irr,
        method = "spearman"
      ),
      cor(
        priority_metric_2425$Metric_B,
        priority_metric_2425$T_irr,
        method = "spearman"
      )
    )
  )

print(rank_concordance_two_product)
```

# 6C. Two-product communication zones

The zone layer is derived from the two continuous Step 11 product-specific metrics, not from
the old raw transmission and severity axes.

The rule is deliberately simple and stated exactly:

- **Transmission-control**: upper tertile of Metric A only.
- **Clinical-preparedness**: upper tertile of Metric B only.
- **Combined priority**: upper tertile of both Metric A and Metric B.
- **Neither upper tertile**: neither product-specific score is in its upper tertile.

The threshold is a communication layer only; all inferential and head-to-head analyses retain
the continuous rankings.

```{r two-product-zones}
cut_A <- quantile(
  priority_metric_2425$Metric_A,
  probs = 2 / 3,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

cut_B_product <- quantile(
  priority_metric_2425$Metric_B,
  probs = 2 / 3,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

priority_metric_2425 <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  mutate(
    high_Metric_A =
      Metric_A >= cut_A,
    high_Metric_B =
      Metric_B >= cut_B_product,
    two_product_zone =
      case_when(
        high_Metric_A &
          high_Metric_B ~
          "Combined priority",
        high_Metric_A &
          !high_Metric_B ~
          "Transmission-control",
        !high_Metric_A &
          high_Metric_B ~
          "Clinical-preparedness",
        TRUE ~
          "Neither upper tertile"
      )
  )

two_product_zone_counts <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  count(
    two_product_zone,
    name = "n_municipalities"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_municipalities =
      100 *
      n_municipalities /
      sum(n_municipalities)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(n_municipalities)
  )

print(two_product_zone_counts)

cat(
  "Metric A upper-tertile cutoff:",
  cut_A,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Metric B upper-tertile cutoff:",
  cut_B_product,
  "\n"
)
```

# 6D. Concordance of zones with the continuous rankings

This table demonstrates that the categorical zones are only a readable summary of the
underlying continuous product-specific scores.

```{r zone-continuous-concordance}
zone_continuous_concordance <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  group_by(
    two_product_zone
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_municipalities = n(),
    median_Metric_A =
      median(
        Metric_A,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    median_Metric_B =
      median(
        Metric_B,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    median_pct_A =
      median(
        pct_A,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    median_pct_B =
      median(
        pct_B,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    median_rank_difference =
      median(
        rank_percentile_difference,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(median_pct_A)
  )

print(zone_continuous_concordance)

top_A_codes <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  filter(high_Metric_A) %>%
  pull(code_muni)

top_B_codes <-
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
  filter(high_Metric_B) %>%
  pull(code_muni)

two_product_overlap <-
  tibble::tibble(
    n_top_A =
      length(top_A_codes),
    n_top_B =
      length(top_B_codes),
    n_overlap =
      length(
        intersect(
          top_A_codes,
          top_B_codes
        )
      ),
    overlap_share_of_A =
      n_overlap / n_top_A,
    overlap_share_of_B =
      n_overlap / n_top_B,
    jaccard =
      n_overlap /
      length(
        union(
          top_A_codes,
          top_B_codes
        )
      )
  )

print(two_product_overlap)
```

# 6E. Two-product maps

The first two panels show percentile ranks of the two continuous metrics. The third panel shows
where the rankings diverge. Positive values indicate relatively higher priority under the current
18-59 product metric; negative values indicate relatively higher priority under the 60+ metric.
The fourth panel is the categorical communication layer.

```{r two-product-maps, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
muni_sf_path <- result_path("muni_sf_2020.rds")

if (!exists("muni_sf")) {
  if (file.exists(muni_sf_path)) {
    muni_sf <- readRDS(muni_sf_path)
  }
}

if (exists("muni_sf")) {

  map_key <- names(muni_sf)[
    grepl(
      "code_muni",
      names(muni_sf),
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ][1]

  if (is.na(map_key) || length(map_key) == 0L) {
    stop(
      "Could not identify code_muni column in muni_sf."
    )
  }

  muni_map <- muni_sf %>%
    mutate(
      code_muni =
        stringr::str_pad(
          substr(
            as.character(
              .data[[map_key]]
            ),
            1,
            6
          ),
          width = 6,
          side = "left",
          pad = "0"
        )
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      priority_metric_2425 %>%
        select(
          code_muni,
          pct_A,
          pct_B,
          rank_percentile_difference,
          two_product_zone
        ),
      by = "code_muni"
    )

  stopifnot(
    sum(
      is.na(
        muni_map$pct_A
      )
    ) == 0L
  )

  p_metric_A <- ggplot(
    muni_map
  ) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(
        fill = pct_A
      ),
      color = NA
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      labels =
        scales::percent_format(
          accuracy = 1
        ),
      name =
        "Priority\npercentile"
    ) +
    labs(
      title =
        "Metric A: ages 18-59",
      subtitle =
        "Current-product expected-burden ranking"
    ) +
    theme_void()

  p_metric_B <- ggplot(
    muni_map
  ) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(
        fill = pct_B
      ),
      color = NA
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      labels =
        scales::percent_format(
          accuracy = 1
        ),
      name =
        "Priority\npercentile"
    ) +
    labs(
      title =
        "Metric B: ages 60+",
      subtitle =
        "Older-adult expected-burden ranking"
    ) +
    theme_void()

  p_metric_difference <- ggplot(
    muni_map
  ) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(
        fill =
          rank_percentile_difference
      ),
      color = NA
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      midpoint = 0,
      labels =
        scales::percent_format(
          accuracy = 1
        ),
      name =
        "A minus B\npercentile"
    ) +
    labs(
      title =
        "Difference in product-specific priority",
      subtitle =
        "Positive = relatively higher under Metric A; negative = relatively higher under Metric B"
    ) +
    theme_void()

  p_two_product_zone <- ggplot(
    muni_map
  ) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(
        fill =
          two_product_zone
      ),
      color = NA
    ) +
    labs(
      title =
        "Two-product communication zones",
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  if (
    requireNamespace(
      "patchwork",
      quietly = TRUE
    )
  ) {
    fig_two_product <-
      (
        p_metric_A |
          p_metric_B
      ) /
      (
        p_metric_difference |
          p_two_product_zone
      )

    print(fig_two_product)

    ggsave(
      file.path(
        results_dir,
        "two_product_priority_maps_2024_2025.png"
      ),
      fig_two_product,
      width = 10,
      height = 8,
      dpi = 600,
      bg = "white"
    )

    ggsave(
      file.path(
        results_dir,
        "two_product_priority_maps_2024_2025.pdf"
      ),
      fig_two_product,
      width = 10,
      height = 8
    )
  } else {
    print(p_metric_A)
    print(p_metric_B)
    print(p_metric_difference)
    print(p_two_product_zone)
  }

} else {
  message(
    "muni_sf_2020.rds not found; tables were created, but map generation was skipped."
  )
}
```

# 6F. Save two-product Step 13 outputs

```{r save-two-product-outputs}
readr::write_csv(
  priority_metric_2425 %>%
    select(
      code_muni,
      region,
      T_irr,
      S_A_18_59,
      S_B_60plus,
      pop_A_18_59,
      pop_B_60plus,
      Metric_A,
      Metric_B,
      rank_A,
      rank_B,
      pct_A,
      pct_B,
      rank_percentile_difference,
```

# 7. Legacy all-age tertile layer retained for backward compatibility

This older all-age transmission/vulnerability classification is retained only so existing downstream validation and archived outputs continue to run. It is **not** the final Step 13 two-product zone definition. The final product-specific communication layer is Section 6C above.

Tertiles are retained only as a communication/classification layer. The underlying transmission, vulnerability, and combined burden scores remain continuous.

```{r tertile-framework}
cut_T <- quantile(priority_metric_2425$T_irr, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_V <- quantile(priority_metric_2425$V_risk, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_B <- quantile(priority_metric_2425$combined_burden, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)

priority_metric_2425 <- priority_metric_2425 %>%
  mutate(
    high_transmission = T_irr >= cut_T,
    high_vulnerability = V_risk >= cut_V,
    high_combined_burden = combined_burden >= cut_B,
    priority_zone = case_when(
      high_transmission & high_vulnerability ~ "High transmission + high severity vulnerability",
      high_transmission & !high_vulnerability ~ "High transmission",
      !high_transmission & high_vulnerability ~ "High severity vulnerability",
      TRUE ~ "Neither upper tertile"
    )
  )

cat("Transmission upper-tertile cutoff:", cut_T, "\n")
cat("Severity-vulnerability upper-tertile cutoff:", cut_V, "\n")
cat("Combined-burden upper-tertile cutoff:", cut_B, "\n\n")

print(priority_metric_2425 %>% count(priority_zone, sort = TRUE))
```

# 8. Validation against exact percentage aged 65+

This analysis tests whether the CFR-weighted severity score adds information beyond the original simple age-structure axis.

```{r validation-age65}
age65_exact <- pop_panel_age %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2024, 2025)) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_65plus = sum(pop[age >= 65], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_total_pop = mean(total_pop),
    mean_pop_65plus = mean(pop_65plus),
    prop_65plus = mean_pop_65plus / mean_total_pop,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

validation_age65 <- priority_metric_2425 %>%
  select(code_muni, V_risk) %>%
  left_join(age65_exact %>% select(code_muni, prop_65plus), by = "code_muni")

rho_age65 <- cor(
  validation_age65$V_risk,
  validation_age65$prop_65plus,
  method = "spearman"
)

cut_v_validation <- quantile(validation_age65$V_risk, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_age65 <- quantile(validation_age65$prop_65plus, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)

validation_age65 <- validation_age65 %>%
  mutate(
    high_V = V_risk >= cut_v_validation,
    high_age65 = prop_65plus >= cut_age65
  )

n_v <- sum(validation_age65$high_V)
n_age65 <- sum(validation_age65$high_age65)
n_overlap_age65 <- sum(validation_age65$high_V & validation_age65$high_age65)
overlap_age65 <- n_overlap_age65 / n_v

cat("Spearman V_risk vs exact %65+:", round(rho_age65, 4), "\n")
cat("V_risk upper tertile:", n_v, "\n")
cat("%65+ upper tertile:", n_age65, "\n")
cat("Overlap:", n_overlap_age65, "\n")
cat("Upper-tertile overlap (%):", round(100 * overlap_age65, 1), "\n")
```

Expected from the current revised data: Spearman rho approximately 0.9673 and upper-tertile overlap approximately 88.0%.

# 9. Sensitivity: exclude 2020-2021 from CFR weights

The primary severity weights use the complete 2016-2025 study period. This sensitivity excludes the COVID-19 pandemic years from the CFR estimation while leaving the 2024-2025 population composition unchanged.

```{r sensitivity-exclude-2020-2021}
cfr_weights_sens <- chik_severity %>%
  group_by(age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    cases_all = n(),
    deaths_all = sum(death, na.rm = TRUE),
    CFR_all = deaths_all / cases_all,
    cases_nonCOVID = sum(!year %in% c(2020, 2021)),
    deaths_nonCOVID = sum(death[!year %in% c(2020, 2021)], na.rm = TRUE),
    CFR_nonCOVID = deaths_nonCOVID / cases_nonCOVID,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

V_sensitivity <- pop_age_2425 %>%
  left_join(cfr_weights_sens, by = "age_band") %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  mutate(total_pop = sum(mean_pop)) %>%
  summarise(
    V_all = sum((mean_pop / total_pop) * CFR_all),
    V_nonCOVID = sum((mean_pop / total_pop) * CFR_nonCOVID),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rho_covid_sens <- cor(
  V_sensitivity$V_all,
  V_sensitivity$V_nonCOVID,
  method = "spearman"
)

cut_all <- quantile(V_sensitivity$V_all, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_nonCOVID <- quantile(V_sensitivity$V_nonCOVID, 2 / 3, na.rm = TRUE)

V_sensitivity <- V_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    high_all = V_all >= cut_all,
    high_nonCOVID = V_nonCOVID >= cut_nonCOVID
  )

n_all <- sum(V_sensitivity$high_all)
n_nonCOVID <- sum(V_sensitivity$high_nonCOVID)
n_overlap_covid <- sum(V_sensitivity$high_all & V_sensitivity$high_nonCOVID)
overlap_covid <- n_overlap_covid / n_all

print(cfr_weights_sens)
cat("Spearman V_all vs V_nonCOVID:", round(rho_covid_sens, 4), "\n")
cat("All-years upper tertile:", n_all, "\n")
cat("Non-COVID upper tertile:", n_nonCOVID, "\n")
cat("Overlap:", n_overlap_covid, "\n")
cat("Upper-tertile overlap (%):", round(100 * overlap_covid, 1), "\n")
```

Expected from the current revised data: Spearman rho approximately 1.000 and upper-tertile overlap approximately 99.9%.

# Interpretation guardrails

- `V_risk` is an age-weighted ecological severity vulnerability score based on observed national age-specific CFRs; it is not an individual-level fatality probability.
- `V_burden` intentionally incorporates municipality population size and therefore should not be used as the severity-vulnerability axis.
- `combined_burden = T_irr * V_burden` is a relative prioritization score, not a calibrated prediction of deaths.
- The 2020-2021 exclusion is a sensitivity analysis; temporal CFR differences should not be attributed causally to COVID-19 without additional evidence.
- Tertiles are a communication layer derived from continuous metrics, not natural biological thresholds.
- The final Step 13 zones use upper tertiles of `Metric_A` and `Metric_B`, not upper tertiles of the raw transmission and severity axes.
- `Metric_A` is restricted to ages 18-59 and is the current-product allocation score.
- `Metric_B` is restricted to ages 60+ and is a projection for an older-adult-eligible product; do not present it as prospectively validated.
- The Metric A versus Metric B difference map is based on percentile-rank differences because raw score magnitudes are not commensurate across the two age windows.

# 12. Head-to-head prioritization-rule comparison

This section compares three deterministic municipality rankings at identical geographic coverage:

1. transmission-only: `T_irr`;
2. age/severity-only: `V_burden`;
3. expected-burden: `combined_burden = T_irr * V_burden`.

A random municipality ordering is included as a reference. The comparison uses observed 2024-2025 confirmed cases and deaths. These are retrospective capture statistics, not estimates of outcomes averted.

Because the revised analytic universe contains 5,570 municipalities, an exact one-third threshold is not an integer. We therefore use `ceiling(5570 / 3) = 1857` municipalities for every deterministic rule.

```{r head-to-head-observed-outcomes}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Observed municipality outcomes, 2024-2025
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
obs_2425 <- Chik_total %>%
  filter(
    CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
    !is.na(DT_SIN_PRI)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)),
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(ID_MUNICIP), 1, 6),
      width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0"
    ),
    age_years_eval = decode_age_years(NU_IDADE_N),
    death_eval = as.integer(as.character(EVOLUCAO) == "2"),
    death_65plus_eval = as.integer(
      as.character(EVOLUCAO) == "2" &
        !is.na(age_years_eval) & age_years_eval >= 65
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(year %in% 2024:2025) %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    cases_2425 = n(),
    deaths_2425 = sum(death_eval, na.rm = TRUE),
    deaths_65plus_2425 = sum(death_65plus_eval, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Mean population aged 65+ in 2024-2025.
pop65_2425 <- pop_panel_age %>%
  filter(year %in% 2024:2025) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year) %>%
  summarise(
    pop_65plus = sum(pop[age >= 65], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pop_65plus_2425 = mean(pop_65plus),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rule_eval_2425 <- priority_metric_2425 %>%
  select(
    code_muni,
    T_irr,
    V_risk,
    V_burden,
    combined_burden
  ) %>%
  left_join(obs_2425, by = "code_muni") %>%
  left_join(pop65_2425, by = "code_muni") %>%
  mutate(
    cases_2425 = tidyr::replace_na(cases_2425, 0L),
    deaths_2425 = tidyr::replace_na(deaths_2425, 0L),
    deaths_65plus_2425 = tidyr::replace_na(deaths_65plus_2425, 0L)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(rule_eval_2425) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(rule_eval_2425$code_muni) == 5570L,
  sum(is.na(rule_eval_2425$mean_pop_65plus_2425)) == 0L,
  sum(rule_eval_2425$cases_2425) == nrow(
    Chik_total %>%
      filter(
        CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
        !is.na(DT_SIN_PRI),
        lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)) %in% 2024:2025
      )
  )
)

cat("2024-2025 observed cases:", sum(rule_eval_2425$cases_2425), "\n")
cat("2024-2025 observed deaths:", sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_2425), "\n")
cat("2024-2025 observed deaths age 65+:",
    sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_65plus_2425), "\n")
```

## 12.1 Matched-coverage top-third comparison

```{r head-to-head-top-third}
N_MUNI <- nrow(rule_eval_2425)
N_SELECT <- ceiling(N_MUNI / 3)

cat("Municipalities in comparison:", N_MUNI, "\n")
cat("Matched top-third selection size:", N_SELECT, "\n")
cat("Coverage (% municipalities):", round(100 * N_SELECT / N_MUNI, 2), "\n")

rule_specs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~rule, ~score_col,
  "Transmission only", "T_irr",
  "Age-structured severity burden", "V_burden",
  "Expected burden", "combined_burden"
)

summarise_top_n <- function(dat, score_col, rule_name, n_select) {
  selected <- dat %>%
    arrange(desc(.data[[score_col]]), code_muni) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_select)

  tibble(
    rule = rule_name,
    n_selected = nrow(selected),
    municipality_coverage = nrow(selected) / nrow(dat),
    cases_captured = sum(selected$cases_2425),
    cases_share = sum(selected$cases_2425) / sum(dat$cases_2425),
    deaths_captured = sum(selected$deaths_2425),
    deaths_share = ifelse(
      sum(dat$deaths_2425) > 0,
      sum(selected$deaths_2425) / sum(dat$deaths_2425),
      NA_real_
    ),
    pop_65plus_covered = sum(selected$mean_pop_65plus_2425),
    pop_65plus_share = sum(selected$mean_pop_65plus_2425) /
      sum(dat$mean_pop_65plus_2425),
    deaths_65plus_captured = sum(selected$deaths_65plus_2425),
    deaths_65plus_share = ifelse(
      sum(dat$deaths_65plus_2425) > 0,
      sum(selected$deaths_65plus_2425) /
        sum(dat$deaths_65plus_2425),
      NA_real_
    )
  )
}

top_third_comparison <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  rule_specs,
  function(rule, score_col) {
    summarise_top_n(
      rule_eval_2425,
      score_col = score_col,
      rule_name = rule,
      n_select = N_SELECT
    )
  }
)

# Random reference at the identical number of municipalities.
set.seed(20261002)
N_RANDOM_TOP <- 2000L

random_top <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(N_RANDOM_TOP), function(b) {
  selected <- rule_eval_2425 %>%
    slice_sample(n = N_SELECT, replace = FALSE)

  tibble(
    cases_captured = sum(selected$cases_2425),
    cases_share = sum(selected$cases_2425) / sum(rule_eval_2425$cases_2425),
    deaths_captured = sum(selected$deaths_2425),
    deaths_share = sum(selected$deaths_2425) / sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_2425),
    pop_65plus_covered = sum(selected$mean_pop_65plus_2425),
    pop_65plus_share = sum(selected$mean_pop_65plus_2425) /
      sum(rule_eval_2425$mean_pop_65plus_2425),
    deaths_65plus_captured = sum(selected$deaths_65plus_2425),
    deaths_65plus_share = ifelse(
      sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_65plus_2425) > 0,
      sum(selected$deaths_65plus_2425) /
        sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_65plus_2425),
      NA_real_
    )
  )
})

random_top_summary <- random_top %>%
  summarise(
    rule = "Random",
    n_selected = N_SELECT,
    municipality_coverage = N_SELECT / N_MUNI,
    cases_captured = median(cases_captured),
    cases_share = median(cases_share),
    deaths_captured = median(deaths_captured),
    deaths_share = median(deaths_share),
    pop_65plus_covered = median(pop_65plus_covered),
    pop_65plus_share = median(pop_65plus_share),
    deaths_65plus_captured = median(deaths_65plus_captured),
    deaths_65plus_share = median(deaths_65plus_share),
    random_cases_share_lo = quantile(cases_share, 0.025),
    random_cases_share_hi = quantile(cases_share, 0.975),
    random_deaths_share_lo = quantile(deaths_share, 0.025),
    random_deaths_share_hi = quantile(deaths_share, 0.975),
    random_deaths65_share_lo = quantile(deaths_65plus_share, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    random_deaths65_share_hi = quantile(deaths_65plus_share, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

head_to_head_top_third <- bind_rows(
  top_third_comparison,
  random_top_summary
)

print(head_to_head_top_third)
```

```{r head-to-head-rank-concordance}
ranking_correlations <- tibble(
```

# 13. Cumulative capture curves

The deterministic curves show retrospective capture under each fixed ranking. The random reference is summarized from repeated random municipality orderings; its shaded band is the 2.5th-97.5th percentile range across random orderings. The deterministic curves are point estimates here; this figure does not substitute for posterior uncertainty propagation in the ranking itself.

```{r cumulative-capture-curves}
make_capture_curve <- function(dat, score_col, rule_name) {

  dat_ranked <- dat %>%
    arrange(desc(.data[[score_col]]), code_muni)

  total_cases <- sum(dat_ranked$cases_2425)
  total_deaths <- sum(dat_ranked$deaths_2425)

  dat_ranked %>%
    mutate(
      rank = row_number(),
      coverage = rank / n(),
      cum_cases_share = cumsum(cases_2425) / total_cases,
      cum_deaths_share = if (total_deaths > 0) {
        cumsum(deaths_2425) / total_deaths
      } else {
        rep(NA_real_, n())
      }
    ) %>%
    select(rank, coverage, cum_cases_share, cum_deaths_share) %>%
    mutate(rule = rule_name)
}

capture_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  rule_specs,
  function(rule, score_col) {
    make_capture_curve(
      rule_eval_2425,
      score_col = score_col,
      rule_name = rule
    )
  }
)

# Random-order uncertainty band. 500 permutations keeps memory/runtime modest.
set.seed(20261002)
N_RANDOM_CURVES <- 500L
n_m <- nrow(rule_eval_2425)

grid_rank <- seq_len(n_m)
random_case_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = N_RANDOM_CURVES, ncol = n_m)
random_death_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = N_RANDOM_CURVES, ncol = n_m)

for (b in seq_len(N_RANDOM_CURVES)) {
  ord <- sample.int(n_m, n_m, replace = FALSE)
  random_case_mat[b, ] <- cumsum(rule_eval_2425$cases_2425[ord]) /
    sum(rule_eval_2425$cases_2425)
  random_death_mat[b, ] <- cumsum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_2425[ord]) /
    sum(rule_eval_2425$deaths_2425)
}

random_curve_band <- tibble(
  rank = grid_rank,
  coverage = grid_rank / n_m,
  cases_mid = apply(random_case_mat, 2, median),
  cases_lo = apply(random_case_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  cases_hi = apply(random_case_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975),
  deaths_mid = apply(random_death_mat, 2, median),
  deaths_lo = apply(random_death_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  deaths_hi = apply(random_death_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

capture_long <- capture_curves %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cum_cases_share, cum_deaths_share),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "captured_share"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = recode(
      outcome,
      cum_cases_share = "Observed cases, 2024-2025",
      cum_deaths_share = "Observed deaths, 2024-2025"
    )
  )

random_band_long <- bind_rows(
  random_curve_band %>%
    transmute(
      coverage,
      outcome = "Observed cases, 2024-2025",
      mid = cases_mid, lo = cases_lo, hi = cases_hi
    ),
  random_curve_band %>%
    transmute(
      coverage,
      outcome = "Observed deaths, 2024-2025",
      mid = deaths_mid, lo = deaths_lo, hi = deaths_hi
    )
)

fig_head_to_head <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = random_band_long,
    aes(x = coverage, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = random_band_long,
    aes(x = coverage, y = mid, linetype = "Random"),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = capture_long,
    aes(x = coverage, y = captured_share, linetype = rule),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = N_SELECT / N_MUNI,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Municipalities prioritized",
    y = "Cumulative share captured",
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "sans", base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(fig_head_to_head)
```

# Additional interpretation guardrails for the rule comparison

- The head-to-head comparison is retrospective: it asks which fixed 2024-2025 ranking captures more of the observed 2024-2025 burden at identical municipality coverage.
- `Age/severity-only` is ranked by `V_burden`, i.e. age-specific observed CFR weighted by municipality population, without the transmission term.
- `Expected-burden` is ranked by `T_irr * V_burden`.
- The random band reflects variation across random municipality orderings only; it is not posterior uncertainty in the INLA-derived transmission surface.
- Captured cases and deaths are observed notified outcomes and must not be described as cases or deaths prevented.
- The revised top-third threshold is 1,857 of 5,570 municipalities (33.34%), replacing the obsolete 1,293-of-3,879 threshold from the earlier restricted-municipality analysis.



# 15. Transmission-population sensitivity analysis
# Compare the age-weighted combined ranking against
# transmission x total population at matched top-third coverage.

```{r transmission-population-sensitivity}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)

# Reuse the existing 2024-2025 evaluation dataset.
pop_sensitivity_data <- rule_eval_2425 %>%
  left_join(
    priority_metric_2425 %>%
      select(code_muni, total_pop),
    by = "code_muni"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    tx_population = T_irr * total_pop
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(pop_sensitivity_data) == 5570L,
  n_distinct(pop_sensitivity_data$code_muni) == 5570L,
  all(is.finite(pop_sensitivity_data$total_pop)),
  all(is.finite(pop_sensitivity_data$tx_population))
)

# Five strategies evaluated at exactly the same coverage.
strategy_cols <- c(
  "Transmission-only" = "T_irr",
  "Age/severity-only" = "V_burden",
  "Expected-burden" = "combined_burden",
  "Population-only" = "total_pop",
  "Transmission x population" = "tx_population"
)

N_SELECT <- ceiling(nrow(pop_sensitivity_data) / 3)

population_sensitivity <- map_dfr(
  names(strategy_cols),
  function(strategy) {

    score_col <- strategy_cols[[strategy]]

    selected <- pop_sensitivity_data %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[score_col]]), code_muni) %>%
      slice_head(n = N_SELECT)

    tibble(
      strategy = strategy,
      n_municipalities = nrow(selected),
      population_covered = sum(selected$total_pop),
      population_pct = 100 *
        sum(selected$total_pop) /
        sum(pop_sensitivity_data$total_pop),
      cases_captured = sum(selected$cases_2425),
      cases_pct = 100 *
        sum(selected$cases_2425) /
        sum(pop_sensitivity_data$cases_2425),
      deaths_captured = sum(selected$deaths_2425),
      deaths_pct = 100 *
        sum(selected$deaths_2425) /
        sum(pop_sensitivity_data$deaths_2425)
    )
  }
)

# Full-precision results for reproducibility.
print(population_sensitivity, n = Inf, width = Inf)

# Comparison of the two combined ranking rules.
rank_comparison <- tibble(
  spearman_rho = cor(
    pop_sensitivity_data$combined_burden,
    pop_sensitivity_data$tx_population,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  top_third_overlap = {
    top_age <- pop_sensitivity_data %>%
      arrange(desc(combined_burden), code_muni) %>%
      slice_head(n = N_SELECT) %>%
      pull(code_muni)

    top_pop <- pop_sensitivity_data %>%
      arrange(desc(tx_population), code_muni) %>%
      slice_head(n = N_SELECT) %>%
      pull(code_muni)

    length(intersect(top_age, top_pop))
  }
) %>%
  mutate(
    top_third_overlap_pct = 100 *
      top_third_overlap / N_SELECT
  )

print(rank_comparison)

# Save separate sensitivity outputs.
write_csv(
  population_sensitivity,
  file.path(
    results_dir,
    "transmission_population_sensitivity_2024_2025.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  rank_comparison,
  file.path(
    results_dir,
    "transmission_population_rank_concordance_2024_2025.csv"
  )
)
```
